the baraita: 'you shall not work with the firstborn of your ox nor shear the firstborn of your flock' (Deut 15:19) -- I have only ox in work and flock in shearing; from where to apply what is said of each to the other? the verse says 'you shall not work ... and you shall not shear'
the verse says 'you shall give him' -- and not for his sack
we require shearing, and there is none [with goats' hair]
who did you hear holds this reasoning? R' Yosei
R' Yosei concedes in what is its usual manner
R' Yehoshua ben Levi: 'to stand to serve' (Deut 18:5) -- a thing fit for service
here too [the first shearing], a thing fit for service
the school of R' Yishmael: sheep whose wool is hard are exempt from the first shearing
as it is said: 'and he was warmed with the shearing of my sheep' (Job 31:20)
one who shears goats is exempt
one baraita: one who shears goats or washes sheep is exempt
another baraita: one who washes sheep is obligated
this [the obligating baraita] is the Rabbis
and that [the exempting baraita] is R' Yosei
'the gleaning of your harvest' (Lev 23:22) -- and not the gleaning of picking
R' Yosei: gleaning is only what comes by harvest
it is all R' Yosei, and this is what it teaches: [not the gleaning of picking] for R' Yosei says gleaning is only what comes by harvest
R' Yosei: 'harvest' -- I have only harvest; one who uproots, from where? the verse says 'to reap'; one who plucks, from where? the verse says 'when you reap'
beds of onions among vegetables -- R' Yosei: pe'a from each one
and the Sages: from one for all
